summary:
Planet X and SPHEREx is an innovative, public-facing web tool designed to make astronomical discovery accessible to everyone. Developed by Team Bugs Bunny for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, our tool tackles the overwhelming scale of NASA’s SPHEREx mission data—which maps the entire sky in 102 near-infrared bands every six months, producing over a billion data points. 

Our platform allows users to input sky coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) to view time-series image sequences of any target patch like a video, making it effortless to spot moving objects such as asteroids, comets, brown dwarfs, and variable stars. Tested successfully on targets like Barnard’s Star and WISE 0855, the tool integrates smart co-addition of detector arrays and Aladin visualization to simplify complex astronomical analysis. By empowering citizen scientists worldwide, this project turns a massive data deluge into an engaging engine for new cosmic discoveries.
details:
Planet X and SPHEREx is an innovative, public-facing web tool designed to make astronomical discovery accessible to everyone.

What it does and how it works: Our platform tackles the massive scale of NASA’s SPHEREx mission data—which maps the entire sky in 102 near-infrared bands every six months. Users can easily input celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) to view time-series image sequences of any target patch like a video. This allows for the effortless detection of moving objects such as asteroids, comets, brown dwarfs, and variable stars through smart co-addition of detector arrays and Aladin Lite integration.

Benefits and Intended Impact: The project bridges raw NASA data with global citizen science. By transforming complex big data into an intuitive, interactive visualization tool, it removes technical barriers and empowers amateur astronomers, students, and space enthusiasts worldwide to actively contribute to real cosmic discoveries.

Tools, Languages, and Software: Developed using Python, Astropy libraries, Aladin Lite for celestial mapping, and web-based front-end technologies to process and display time-series astronomical data efficiently.

Creativity and Team Considerations: Our team focused on reimagining multi-band infrared sky surveys as dynamic time-lapse video feeds. We carefully considered user accessibility, accurate coordinate mapping (RA/Dec), processing performance across 102 infrared bands, and validated our tool against rigorous real-world test targets such as Barnard’s Star and WISE 0855.
